hero.title: GalaxyMVC - PHP Framework
hero.tagline: Lightweight MVC framework built from scratch with clean architecture

sections.title: The Challenge
sections.content: Many PHP developers struggle to understand MVC architecture when learning frameworks like Laravel or Symfony due to their complexity. The goal was to create a minimal MVC framework that clearly demonstrates the pattern without magic methods or hidden complexity, making it perfect for education and small projects.

sections.title: Technical Approach
sections.content: Built a clean MVC implementation from scratch using only PHP's core features. The framework includes a custom router that parses URLs, an autoloader following PSR-4 standards, a PDO database wrapper for secure queries, and a simple view system with template inheritance.

subsections.title: Routing Architecture
subsections.content: Implemented a regex-based router that converts URLs to controller/method calls, supporting dynamic parameters and maintaining clean URLs without exposing file structure.

subsections.title: Database Abstraction
subsections.content: Created a PDO wrapper that provides a fluent interface for database operations while preventing SQL injection through prepared statements.

sections.title: Implementation Details
sections.content: The framework follows a traditional MVC pattern where requests hit a front controller, get routed to appropriate controllers, which interact with models for data and return views. The entire codebase is under 1000 lines, making it easy to understand and modify.

sections.title: Results & Impact
sections.content: GalaxyMVC became a valuable learning tool for understanding MVC architecture. Its simplicity makes it perfect for teaching, prototyping, and building small applications where larger frameworks would be overkill. The clean codebase serves as a reference implementation of MVC patterns.
metrics: Sub-50ms response time for basic pages
